title: The Indistractable Workplace
coreMove: Turn attention-friendly culture into shared routines that make focused work, responsiveness, and recovery predictable.
sourcePressure: The chapter describes operational habits of a healthier workplace built from explicit coordination, routines, and permission across channels.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would imagine a utopian quiet office instead of concrete shared practices people can rely on.

hook: The Indistractable Workplace as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: regional pathology lab building a specimen-review routine
exampleSpecs.audience: lab manager turning culture diagnosis into daily practice
exampleSpecs.stakes: specimen accuracy depends on predictable quiet and escalation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she posts review hours, escalation codes, and a handoff ritual on the specimen bench
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A specimen cassette rack sits beside an escalation code card.

exampleSpecs.domain: newspaper copy desk coordinating print close
exampleSpecs.audience: copy chief balancing focus and urgent corrections
exampleSpecs.stakes: front-page errors and late changes both need rules
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he creates a close-window rule where only named corrections break the copy block
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A page proof lies under a close-window rule strip.

exampleSpecs.domain: solar installation crew planning roof days
exampleSpecs.audience: crew lead making attention routines survive field work
exampleSpecs.stakes: falls and wiring mistakes rise with unclear channels
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the crew names the radio phrase that stops work and the tablet queue that can wait
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A roof harness tag hangs beside a radio phrase card.

exampleSpecs.domain: public library reference team covering deep research requests
exampleSpecs.audience: reference manager building focus without abandoning patrons
exampleSpecs.stakes: patrons need both availability and serious research
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, every desk ping breaks research; after, one librarian covers walkups while another gets a protected archive block
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An archive request slip sits beside a desk-coverage token.

exampleSpecs.domain: manufacturing maintenance team after too many hallway asks
exampleSpecs.stakes: urgent breakdowns and routine fixes need different handling
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he replaces hallway requests with a triage board and a genuine breakdown alarm
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A triage board magnet rests beside a breakdown alarm key.

exampleSpecs.domain: remote nonprofit fundraising team planning donor outreach
exampleSpecs.stakes: donor calls need focus while crisis exceptions remain possible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sets call blocks, response windows, and one crisis channel in the team handbook
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A donor call sheet sits under a response-window bookmark.
